subject.title: gateway tool not available to external-provider agent sessions

question: Should explicitly allowlisted `gateway` be exposed to non-embedded external-provider owner sessions such as xAI/Grok, or remain limited to local/webchat/control-plane contexts?
rationale: The source suggests explicit `alsoAllow` should work and `gateway` is not webchat-only, but making that true for external-provider sessions exposes config and restart authority through a security-sensitive tool.

options.title: Honor explicit gateway allowlist
options.body: Treat this as a bug when an owner session explicitly allows `gateway`, add xAI/Grok proof, and keep the existing policy/authorization gates intact.

options.title: Limit gateway to local control surfaces
options.body: Document the limitation and add a clear diagnostic so external-provider sessions do not appear misconfigured when `gateway` is intentionally withheld.

options.title: Add a stricter opt-in boundary
options.body: Require a new reviewed security policy before external-provider sessions can receive `gateway`, with migration/docs/proof for the new operator action.

recommendation.title: Honor explicit gateway allowlist
recommendation.body: Treat this as a bug when an owner session explicitly allows `gateway`, add xAI/Grok proof, and keep the existing policy/authorization gates intact.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest routing candidate from recent ownership of the affected agent/gateway tool policy path and the security-sensitive nature of the decision.
